shipped_rows.title_o: A direct interview family study of obsessive–compulsive disorder. I

blind_target.evidence_quote: Overall findings of our first direct interview family study of obsessive–compulsive disorder (OCD) indicated that OCD is familial. In this replication study, we carefully examined the role of informant data in ascertaining OCD in relatives.
blind_target.outcome_quote: When relative diagnoses were derived without the benefit of proband informant reports, no evidence of familial OCD transmission was found. When diagnoses were made including information from the proband about the relative, evidence of familial OCD was found, but only when the diagnostic threshold was lowered to include cases with probable OCD or OCD symptoms.
blind_target.outcome_reasoning: Original familial association is stated. Authors report no familial evidence under one diagnostic procedure and evidence under another with a lowered threshold, and explicitly describe their results as inconsistent. Less robust support does not itself cause the mixed verdict; the contrasted presence and absence of the finding does.

luna_triage.reason: The abstract says this is a replication of the authors’ first direct-interview family study and states that OCD was familial, but the supplied abstract does not identify that first paper by citation or title and contains no reference list. Although shipped row 886 has a similar Part I title and overlapping authors, the allowed source evidence does not establish that it is the same original. Need the full paper/reference identity or authoritative source link.
